messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- The failing test builds an OptionGroup containing two options that have only long names (no short names) using OptionBuilder.withLongOpt("foo").create() and OptionBuilder.withLongOpt("bar").create(). It then parses "--bar" and expects group.getSelected() to return "bar".
- OptionGroup.addOption(Option) stores options in an internal map keyed by option.getKey(). Option.getKey() returns longOpt when opt is null, so the group’s map is correctly keyed as "foo" and "bar" for pure long options.
- OptionGroup.getSelected() simply returns the String field selected.
- The bug report states that “If the selected option hasn’t a short name, group.setSelected(option) has no effect.” This matches the test failure: after parsing "--bar", group.getSelected() is not "bar".
- The only plausible way for setSelected to have “no effect” for pure long options is if OptionGroup.setSelected(Option) sets the selected field from option.getOpt(), which is null for options without a short name, instead of using a stable identifier like option.getKey() (or option.getLongOpt() when opt is null).
- Therefore, during parsing, when the parser identifies the "--bar" option and calls group.setSelected(option), selected is assigned null due to option.getOpt() being null. As a result, group.getSelected() returns null, causing the test to fail.

Root cause:
- OptionGroup.setSelected(Option) records the selection using Option.getOpt() (short name) rather than using Option.getKey() (which returns the long name when there is no short name). This makes selection tracking ineffective for options that have only a long name.
